memories.content: The user's available days and times vary by week, making it difficult to apply last month's free time directly to the next appointment.
The user once canceled an appointment booked for the same weekday as in the previous month.
When asked again about availability just before booking, the user provided three free times for that week.
On a day with two consecutive morning appointments, the user ate lunch at 3 p.m.
On a day the user left an hour between appointments, they ate while traveling.
After seeing a private reason written directly in a calendar title, the user removed the wording.
The user checked that a calendar-sharing screen showed only the time and hid the details.
When evening plans on the same day must change, the user's mother wants advance notice on the weekend morning.
The local agent cannot know the private reason for unavailability from the unavailable time alone.
The user's shared calendar does not automatically reserve travel time between events.
The user stores prepared meals on the second shelf of the freezer.
The user went to the market without a shopping list and bought onions that were already at home.
On a day the user shopped after checking a refrigerator photo, they did not make a duplicate purchase.
On a day the user made a spicy stew, they left part of one bowl uneaten.
The next time the user cooked it, they used half as much chili powder and finished the meal.
When cooking with their younger brother, the user assigned the cooking sequence only verbally and they did the same task twice.
The next time, the user and their younger brother split ingredient preparation and heat control and finished the meal 20 minutes earlier.
When cooking together, the user's younger brother prefers to divide the cooking and dishwashing roles in advance.
The local agent can compare responses across several meals, but it cannot conclude from one unfinished food item that the user dislikes that ingredient.
The condition of frozen prepared food may vary with its packaging and storage duration.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate operational domains with no claim-level overlap: the reference concerns scheduling and calendar handling, while the compared frame concerns food storage, shopping, meal preferences, and shared cooking. All information is independently useful and neither side contradicts or qualifies the other.

relations.reason: Variable schedules, a cancellation after reusing a weekday, and successfully obtaining current free times jointly support one scheduling-specific claim absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Weekly availability should be confirmed near booking rather than inferred from a prior month.

relations.reason: The late lunch after consecutive appointments and eating while traveling despite a one-hour gap are complementary observations about appointment-day meal disruption, with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Appointment timing and spacing can disrupt when and where the user eats.

relations.reason: Removing sensitive title wording and verifying that sharing reveals only time jointly express one calendar-privacy practice absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: The user avoids exposing private reasons in shared calendar details.

relations.reason: This is an independent family coordination preference with no corresponding claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The user's mother expects weekend-morning advance notice when same-day evening plans must change.

relations.reason: This is a calendar-specific inference limitation, operationally separate from the compared frame's food-preference inference limitation.
relations.summary: An unavailable time alone does not reveal its private reason to the local agent.

relations.reason: This identifies an independent scheduling-system limitation not addressed in the compared frame.
relations.summary: The shared calendar does not automatically reserve travel time between events.

relations.reason: This is a standalone food-location fact with no corresponding scheduling or calendar claim in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Prepared meals are stored on the freezer's second shelf.

relations.reason: The duplicate onion purchase without a list and the successful refrigerator-photo check are contrasting observations supporting one shopping-preparation claim absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: Checking available household inventory before shopping can prevent duplicate purchases.

relations.reason: The unfinished spicy serving and later completed reduced-chili meal form one meal-adjustment observation with no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Using less chili powder was associated with the user finishing a previously over-spicy stew.

relations.reason: Verbal-only sequencing produced duplicated work, while divided preparation and heat-control roles improved completion time, consistent with the brother's stated preference for advance role division.
relations.summary: Dividing cooking responsibilities in advance improves coordination when the user cooks with their younger brother.

relations.reason: This is a food-preference inference rule, distinct from the reference frame's calendar-specific inability to infer private reasons.
relations.summary: The local agent needs evidence across meals and cannot infer an ingredient dislike from one unfinished item.

relations.reason: This independent food-storage qualification has no matching operational claim in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Frozen prepared-food condition may depend on packaging and storage duration.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers freezer storage, inventory checks, adapting spice levels, coordinating shared cooking, limits on inferring food dislikes, and storage-condition variability.
reports.reference_only: The reference describes variable availability, appointment effects on meals, calendar privacy, family notice expectations, limits on inferring private reasons, and absent travel-time reservations.
